title: PACEgame A Python toolkit for inspecting continuous time entry and signalling models
author_note: Author names, affiliations, corresponding author and contact details require author confirmation before submission.
abstract: PACEgame is a Python toolkit for inspecting continuous-time entry and signalling models. It connects replaceable demand lifecycles and share rules to symbolic payoffs, sequential numerical searches, local diagnostics and sampled claim reports. Users can compare conditional strategy scenarios, differentiate resolved candidate outcomes and export version-bound evidence. The package includes two demand lifecycles, two share rules, three model factories, a command-line interface and executable examples. Numerical states distinguish model corners, fixed decisions and exhausted computational searches. Required checks expose missing evidence; isolated share sensitivity excludes cost-only responses. Claims require accounted samples, and non-finite differences cannot establish signs. A supplied costless-signal example reaches a finite payoff limit, showing why a search cap does not prove divergence. Stock, cost, signal-bound and readiness-lag variants illustrate how assumptions change candidate rankings and sampled propositions. Typed cache keys preserve model state, and derivative claims bind their stated player. Retained parameters, objectives and candidate values align search and necessary derivatives. Domain conversion exposes coordinate precision loss. Retained payoff differences guard tested cancellation. Structural symbols and players remain distinct. Retained endpoints, tolerance signs and finite-real payoffs protect reported candidates. Validation includes 493 tests, independent quadrature and analytic sequential, crossing and fixed-domain examples. General-horizon checks align entry domains, costs and cumulative-demand bounds. The software is intended for researchers, reviewers and instructors working with stylized timing models. Finite searches, local diagnostics and sampled claims do not certify global optimality, continuous-domain propositions or Nash equilibrium. The delivered archive supports review; public archival identifiers and confirmed author declarations remain pending.
keywords: entry timing; signalling; sequential decisions; symbolic computation; numerical verification; research software
highlights: Combines replaceable demand primitives with symbolic timing-model payoffs.
Distinguishes fixed decisions, numerical corners and unresolved searches.
Retains parameter and candidate values before search and necessary derivatives.
Checks retained joint curvature at interior and critical boundary points.
Provides source, wheel, offline core dependencies and reproducibility records.
sections: 1. Motivation and significance

Researchers studying platform entry, deployment timing and preannouncement often integrate a demand path, differentiate its payoff and compare four policy scenarios. A stationary point does not establish a feasible maximum. It can lie outside the horizon, represent a minimum or omit a relevant corner. A numerical substitute creates additional questions: which points could be evaluated, whether the search stopped at a computational budget, and whether a purported proposition was tested everywhere requested.

PACEgame connects reusable lifecycles, demand-share rules and decision ownership to payoffs, domains, candidate searches and reports. Users can change demand assumptions within one inspection procedure. Its contribution is an auditable computational workflow rather than a new entry-timing theorem.

Existing tools have complementary strengths. Gambit supports construction and analysis of finite extensive and strategic games [1], including sequential representations. Nashpy computes equilibria for two-player normal-form games [2]. QuantEcon provides computational economics routines, including discrete dynamic programming [3]. SymPy supplies symbolic algebra and calculus [4]. PACEgame combines symbolic continuous-time demand integrals with model-specific bounded searches and sampled propositions. It does not replace these tools or establish superior equilibrium algorithms. Table 3 states the comparison’s scope.
Version 0.2.11 retains counterexamples to finite-limit mislabelling, unevaluable claims and unsuccessful benchmarks. Checks establish covered behavior; unchecked properties remain unresolved.

Researchers, instructors and reviewers are the intended users. Inputs specify stylized models; empirical adoption or policy applications require separate calibration. External uptake and published companion-study replication are unverified. The unavailable companion study remains a clearly identified legacy claim inventory.
2. Software description
2.1. Architecture and model contract

The package contains four layers (Fig. 1). Core classes define demand segments, installed stocks, demand shares, strategies and costs. Model factories compose these primitives. The solver retains actual numerical parameter values before substituting into symbolic payoffs and searches according to the declared move order. Analysis modules assemble candidate rankings, finite-difference responses and claim reports. Plotting is an optional presentation layer; all numerical operations use Python and SymPy without importing Matplotlib [5].

A Lifecycle implements segments, stock_at and capacity. Segments store intervals and symbolic demand integrals. TwoPhase represents constant arrivals followed by maturity; Logistic measures adoption from a common time-zero origin. A ShareRule allocates arriving users from installed stock. Proportional uses relative quality and a stock-dependent network term; Logit uses exponential weights. Parameters are stylized, not empirical estimates. capacity bounds cumulative endogenous demand, excluding externally created stock. TwoPhase uses sigma(growth_end×horizon−growth_end²/2); Logistic uses the loose bound ceiling×horizon. A carried stock contributes at most stock×horizon to integrated demand. This diagnostic envelope does not impose customer conservation.

Game binds primitives to distinct player identities, independent scalar entry, signal and time Symbols, costs and flags. External primitive parameter symbols cannot alias structural symbols; public computation rechecks mutable state. Gross payoff is one quarter of integrated demand. Timing cost is kappa_t(1−own_entry/horizon); quadratic signal cost is kappa_d×signal²/2. Both are nonnegative on the domain; timing preserves the unit-horizon specification. The pioneer enters at zero. RF assigns the focal signal before rival follower entry; RL jointly assigns signal and follower entry to the focal player. DF and DL omit signal. Labels define conditional scenarios with fixed role rules. A mechanically matched rival signal changes stocks but creates neither an independent rival decision nor its signalling cost. Quality keys must name actual players; omitted quality defaults to one. Unknown keys reject. Interchangeability uses effective qualities; role_conflict remains descriptive.

Primitive coefficients accept expressions; only free Symbols enter inventories. Name collisions reject. Parameters and evaluated coefficients pass retained finite-real and sign checks before conversion. Nonzero values converting to zero or nonfinite binary64 raise ValueError; zero costs remain valid. Inputs are preserved before substitution. Require zero ≤ entry_floor ≤ growth_end ≤ horizon and positive horizon; Logistic uses horizon as growth_end. Invalid methods, budgets and strategies reject. Bounds must be independent numerical intervals; endpoints are retained separately before subtraction. Float atoms in expressions and substitutions become their actual binary rationals before arithmetic or differentiation. This cannot infer decimals or recover previously lost terms. Binary64 endpoint conversion must respect absolute tolerance 1e-9, including singletons, and distinguish nonzero intervals. Unsafe conversion raises BoundsPrecisionError; required precision warnings prevent completion. Narrow representable intervals remain supported. Decision-dependent domains and custom demand restrictions remain outside the contract.

Symbolic payoff construction is memoized using primitive state, full strategy flags and the time symbol. Subclass payoff overrides remain part of the solver contract. Examples and regression tests ship in the wheel for execution outside a checkout.

Cache keys preserve primitive class, public dictionary/dataclass/slot fields, and recursively typed state. Dictionary/set order is irrelevant; sequences stay ordered. Integer/string keys and same-named Symbols with different assumptions remain distinct. Supported state comprises scalar/SymPy values and acyclic containers; hidden, cyclic or opaque extensions need explicit representation and invalidate after mutation. Custom parameter inventories must match expressions.
2.2. Candidate search and diagnostics

The numerical path performs backward recursion over the declared stages. At each stage, an objective evaluation includes the continuation selected by later stages. One-dimensional searches scan a grid and refine a neighborhood; joint choices use a product grid followed by coordinate refinement. Model corners are included. This procedure produces numerical candidates, not a global certificate: narrow peaks, multiple separated maxima and discontinuous follower responses can defeat the finite scan. Every result retains an explicit search-assurance warning.

For an open upper domain, a doubling probe supplies a finite search box. Exhausting that budget produces the search-limit state. The state is unresolved: finite observations cannot distinguish a distant finite maximum, an unattained finite supremum and an infinite payoff. The current numerical routine does not infer unbounded payoff from such a probe. Search-limit flags from discarded follower continuations are not accumulated into the selected continuation. Invalid or unresolved candidates cannot participate in payoff comparisons or comparative statics, and a ranking with no valid candidate returns no best label.

Tolerances pass retained finite-real and nonnegative-sign checks; nonzero binary64 underflow or overflow rejects. Diagnostics validate coordinate/bounds coverage and known kind labels against actual positions. Omitted labels are inferred. Corner classification, derivative evaluation and membership use the same retained candidate. Membership and payoff ceilings retain the admitted tolerance. Net, supplied gross and every declared payoff_for owner objective require finite-real evidence before conversion or derivative skipping; known invalid values fail and unknown values prevent completion, including fixed and earlier-stage decisions. Derivative heuristics still use numerical approximations. Checks cover bounds, reported-payoff finiteness, independent final-value payoff agreement, supplied gross payoff and requested ceilings. Ceilings compare retained payoff-minus-limit differences with unchanged absolute tolerances: 1e-9 in check_point and 1e-12 in Bounded. FeasibilityReport.ok excludes violations; complete also requires necessary verdicts. Unavailable required bounds, ceilings, curvature or payoff comparisons prevent ranking. Omitted gross is skipped rather than replaced by net profit, which may be negative. Fixed decisions have no one-sided test. Equal declared objectives receive shared joint Hessian checks at interior points and supported boundaries; distinct objectives remain separate. Boundary curvature covers at most two critical feasible directions, including a remaining coordinate after fixed neighbors are removed. Earlier stages, fixed coordinates and strict boundary-gradient directions are excluded. Hessians use retained signs, strict adaptive precision and squared cone comparisons. Larger cones remain incomplete; flat curvature leaves higher orders unresolved. Raw leader partials are withheld for reduced objectives. These are necessary local conditions. Final-point payoff agreement does not prove objective accuracy across the search domain.

Parameter-retained objectives enter compiled and cancelled evaluation; symbolic fallback retains trial coordinates. Compiled binary64 arithmetic can still round or cancel. Failed inexpensive routes have bounded retry intervals; the final route remains available after local failure. Coverage counts attempted evaluations, failures and rescues, including repeated calls; it is not unique-domain coverage. Local stationarity polishing uses the retained objective and accepts only close, feasible corrections without decreasing its evaluated value. The share diagnostic isolates explicit share-rule sensitivity through a chain rule, holding decisions, installed stocks, lifecycle and costs fixed. Independent stock and share placeholders prevent a shared parameter’s cost or demand path from being mistaken for share activity. A custom payoff or share path must declare a share_sensitivity hook; otherwise this diagnostic is unknown. A 1e-12 absolute sensitivity tolerance distinguishes activity, numerical inactivity and unknown results. A nonzero result establishes local activity. All-zero sensitivity falsifies that activity claim without invalidating the payoff; unavailable sensitivity yields no verdict. None establishes the absence of competition globally.
2.3. Claim reports and interfaces

Users express comparisons, interiority, feasibility, magnitude bounds and derivative signs as claims. Sign accepts d pi_<player> / d <parameter>, binding either current player’s payoff. Unknown targets, parameters, strategies and malformed expressions reject before sampling. Decision responses remain available through derivative(quantity=<decision>), outside Sign; payoff gaps require quantity="payoff". Claim iterables, including generators, are materialized once. Reports separately count passes, failures, skips and computation errors, retaining parameters and reasons. Feasible cannot pass after a failed solve or incomplete required checks. Interior concerns a whole valid candidate and skips unresolved or invalid parents, even if a follower coordinate has an interior label. This scope does not assert a separately conditional follower fact. A claim holds only when every requested sample receives a verdict and none fails. Report.ok excludes errors and counterexamples; Report.complete also excludes skips and requires each claim’s counts to equal the requested point count; an empty or partially evaluated report cannot be complete. Finite-grid success is evidence on samples, not a regional theorem.

The Python entry point rank_strategies names the actual comparison. equilibrium remains a compatibility alias, and output always states that it is not Nash-certified. Sweeps consume a nonempty unique admitted strategy iterable once; empty values return an empty list after pool validation. Sweeps, verification axes and command-line overrides reject unknown parameter names. For backward compatibility, Game.numeric ignores inactive names in dictionaries containing alternative model switches. Users needing strict name checks should use the documented interfaces rather than infer strictness from that conversion helper.

Comparative statics use finite differences of resolved candidates, recording a feasible one-sided stencil when central perturbation leaves the parameter domain. Each solution retains payoffs with its own parameters and candidate. Ranking, ties, dominance, crossings and payoff differences subtract retained operands before conversion; float payoffs remain display values. Unknown comparisons prevent completion or produce explicit errors/skips. Absolute dominance and tie thresholds remain 1e-12 and 1e-9. Difference denominators, numerators and final slopes must be finite. Nonzero result underflow or overflow raises a numerical-range error, recorded as a claim error without a sign verdict; the sign accessor also rejects non-finite slopes. Kinks and regime changes need step-size checks. Threshold routines retain sampled zeros between opposite nonzero signs and refine direct sign-change brackets. A sampled zero run returns a representative point, not a unique transition boundary; endpoint ties and touching zeros alone are not strict reversals. None means no strict crossing was detected at that resolution. Command-line operations return zero for complete valid output, one for counterexamples or unresolved output, and two for malformed input or verification errors; sweep follows the same contract.
3. Illustrative examples

The archive includes source, an installable wheel and upstream core dependency wheels for offline installation. Plotting is optional. README.md documents installation, testing and figures. The example constructs the stock-cost variant and prints its conditional candidate ranking.
code

python -m pip install '.[figures]'
python -m pacegame.cli solve preannounce_entry --repair
python examples/validate_release.py validation
python examples/make_figures.py figures
python examples/validate_audit_021.py validation
python examples/validate_audit_022.py validation
python examples/validate_audit_023.py validation

python examples/validate_audit_028.py validation

python examples/validate_audit_0211.py validation

The baseline point uses sigma=0.1, phi=0.85 and growth_end=0.3. Silent labels DF and DL choose immediate follower entry and each yield 0.0031875. Signalling labels reach the numerical search limit and are excluded. Independent symbolic evaluation at entry zero gives a finite limit of 0.006375 as the signal tends to infinity. The counterexample corrects the former infinite-payoff interpretation; finite search remains explicitly unresolved.

The stock-cost variant carries follower stock into demand, makes the signal accrue during the wait and charges quadratic cost with kappa_d=0.05. Its RL candidate has signal approximately 1.05, entry 0.3 and net payoff 0.0275625. RF, DF and DL yield 0.0031875. Entry is an upper corner and local network-parameter sensitivity vanishes for RL there. The result describes signal-created stock in this stylized specification; customer conservation is not imposed. It cannot be interpreted as observed adoption or calibrated economic welfare.

Adding the chosen signal ceiling of 0.1 changes RL to an upper-corner signal with payoff 0.005. Its candidate ranking remains highest at the example point, but its interior-signal claim changes. Fig. 2 and Table 4 disclose both magnitudes. A readiness lag of 0.1 instead gives DF payoff 0.004383464 and DL payoff 0.001991536, while RL still selects the growth-end corner. This lag creates a silent pioneer window; it does not force every strategy to regain a locally active share channel.

All variants use the same six claims over nine points: sigma spans 0.05–0.4 and phi spans 0.3–0.95 at three values per axis. The stock-cost variant passes four claims and fails two at every sample. Adding the ceiling passes three and fails three; adding readiness lag passes five and fails one. The baseline skips four claims involving unresolved signalling candidates, including both interiority checks, and fails the silent strict comparison and feasibility claim. Complete counts and reasons are stored in release_validation.json. These are sampled outcomes rather than general dominance proofs (Fig. 3).

Independent 40-digit quadrature integrates fixed demand segments for 18 model–strategy combinations and both players; its maximum difference from reported net payoffs is approximately 2.6×10⁻¹⁷. Two additional horizon cases are cross-checked in audit_021_acceptance.json. A sequential analytic example has follower response e=d/2 and reduced leader objective d/2−d²/2. Its solution d=0.5, e=0.25 and leader payoff 0.125 matches numerical choices within 10⁻⁶. It also demonstrates why a raw leader partial need not vanish at the correct reduced-objective choice.

Source, full-wheel and core-only environments each run 493 tests: 450 parent cases and 43 new regressions. Owner-payoff admission covers fixed, interior, lower-corner and skipped-stage paths: known complex, NaN and infinite values fail; unknown values remain incomplete. Different finite objectives and negative nets remain valid. Fixed-candidate payoffs A and A+1 retain gap 1 at A=2^53, 2^60 and 10^20 in either strategy order. RL wins, strict dominance passes and reversed weak dominance fails. A+phi-1/2 crosses A at phi=0.5; the constrained derivative of A+sigma is 1. Controls cover representable offsets, absolute tolerances, player targets and separately bound candidates and perturbations. Prior interval, coefficient, retained-ceiling and Hessian controls remain valid; unstable search candidates remain excluded. Twelve exporters exercise 41 groups in all three environments, with 17 metadata labels matching the depth report. Independent public-interface probes reproduce the parent defects and accept the revision. Hosted CI remains unexecuted.

Historical v0.2.10 benchmark records successful subprocess wall times, including startup, in repeated rounds, with raw repetitions, medians, ranges and host-load observations. This revision does not add timing; shared-host measurements do not certify isolation or comparative speed. Reproduction pins and records agree on SymPy 1.14.0, mpmath 1.3.0, Matplotlib 3.10.8 and NumPy 2.3.5. Core offline installation excludes plotting; a separate lock records the optional environment. Pins do not guarantee bitwise results across hardware.
4. Impact

The demonstrated benefit is a more inspectable analytical workflow. A user can connect the supplied model, numerical candidate, local diagnostics and sampled proposition through one versioned output record. The baseline finite-asymptote example and the deliberately broken-payoff regression establish concrete cases where the revised reporting changes the conclusion available to a reader. The benchmark-failure regression prevents an unsuccessful program from producing a plausible performance observation. These are verified behaviors in the delivered release, not evidence of external uptake.

Potential reuse includes teaching entry-timing trade-offs, checking the consequences of stock and cost assumptions, and reviewing symbolic claims against constrained numerical candidates. Switching from TwoPhase to Logistic or from Proportional to Logit exercises the same interfaces. Asymmetric quality can expose locally active parameters away from a boundary. Extensions retain diagnostics only when they satisfy the documented model and parameter contracts; a custom economic specification remains the modeller’s responsibility.

Practical reproducibility comes from the installable wheel, offline core dependency set, shipped examples, environment records and checksums. This supports artifact review without pretending that a locally delivered archive is a permanent public repository. Before journal submission, the authors must supply verified identities and support contact, publish a frozen source version and permanent archive, and confirm declarations. Those identifiers are explicitly pending in the metadata tables. Claims of citations, download counts, course adoption or industrial use require evidence that was not supplied.

Limitations include finite heuristic searches, local diagnostics, rectangular bounds, fixed two-player roles and uncalibrated demand. Feasibility cannot remove these limits. Full simultaneous interactions, certified global optimization and continuous-domain proofs remain outside the release. Detailed audit evidence accompanies the package.
5. Conclusions

PACEgame 0.2.11 provides a reusable route from continuous-time demand primitives to symbolic payoffs, constrained numerical candidates and sampled claim reports. Explicit fixed-domain, required-check and sensitivity states prevent distinct computations from being reported as the same outcome. Typed cache state, consistent retained parameters, candidates and derivatives, independent structural symbols, distinct players, retained joint interior and critical feasible curvature and accounted samples align outputs with their meaning. Retained endpoints, tolerance signs, owner-payoff admission and retained inter-candidate differences prevent these audited false acceptances. Source and wheel regressions, quadrature and analytic counterchecks support the covered examples; final-point agreement does not certify all search arithmetic. The software remains an inspection toolkit with stated limits; it does not certify global solutions or full Nash strategy interactions.

Future work includes search refinement, follower ties, decision-dependent domains and independent global comparisons. Empirical applications need calibration. Confirmed authors, declarations and permanent public identifiers remain necessary before submission.
